# Independent audit: same-separator full-space log flux

Target: `candidate 8f0725a173821a00`, Sections 1--7.

Result: PASS within the explicitly regular, singleton-contact, unpenalized
and physically addable joint-direction scope. No algebraic or geometric
repair identified. The note does not solve the remaining nonaffine torque
or identify the surface and volume martingales.

## 1. Feasibility and the common separator

The parameter directions in Section 2 have a finite concave extension
after adding a multiple of the same finite-PL L. Positivity on a common
neighborhood permits these directions simultaneously with the stated
signed global-cut body paths. This is a genuine joint feasible cone, not
an assumed product of independently formal derivatives. The regular
contact response is linear in both directions, so separation from the
open improvement orthant is legitimate without a closed-image assertion.

The positive-Delta claim in the mixed atomic case correctly retains the
atomic hinge action in the SAME physical cone and the numerical count
condition; it is also explicitly allowed as a hypothesis. No regularity
of arbitrary bad minimizers is inferred. Globally finite convex parameter
tests suffice for the finite-source coupling proof because its only
separating tests are finite maxima of affine functions.

For inward speed v, the log normalization derivative is +s(v), since
the unnormalized log integral has derivative -integral log L v and its
old value is zero. Thus (8) has the correct +s and -H signs. The energy,
mass and covariance terms combine to the exact coefficient
-(N+2)D/(2NM) in (10). The -h(Y_i)/(N L_i)+H/N terms give precisely
the volume convex order with the SAME e_i=eta_i delta_i, not a new
parameter-only choice of weights.

## 2. Labeled moments and force

Finite-PL contact and absolute continuity of the volume rows force a
unique continuous gradient at every positive source; equal base-only
planes are correctly permitted. The row barycenter gives all the tensor
identities (17), by testing each coordinate of w with the appropriate
gradient-label component. The L moment gives the original-volume identity
(16); it must not be replaced by an unweighted first-moment identity.

The force (19) has the correct signs and factors. On K intersect H the
internal cut normal is -u/|u|, so the boundary-of-K cap force is +S_z u.
The energy kernel contributes -N E_i a_i before its prefactor e_i/(N E_i).
The centered covariance quadratic contributes zero vector force, and
-kappa log L contributes -kappa integral grad log L. The first two labeled
moments then cancel exactly the source c_i/(N L_i) terms in the total
force and base torque (20).

## 3. Independent continuous-tensor computation

For a scalar boundary density Z,

    integral_boundary Z X tensor n
      =Id integral_K Z + integral_K X tensor grad Z.

For the actual cap selector, the first term is its raw cap mass times
Id and the second contribution can equivalently be written as the
section first moment tensor u. The raw Q terms of W cancel -beta M Id,
including atomic rows. Using the ACTUAL section centroid in (4), the
remaining cap contribution is

    sum_i e_i[y_i tensor(a_i+c_i/(N L_i))-Sigma C_i^u].

For the energy kernel, (5) gives
e_i Id/N-e_i y_i tensor a_i. For the covariance quadratic, its integral
is Delta/2 because Gamma(u_ij)=1, and its derivative tensor is
sum_i e_i Sigma C_i^u. This computation uses only WITHIN-fiber centered
second moments; there is no hidden assumption on the graph g_z.

The constant contributes -(N+2)Delta Id/(2N). The logarithmic scalar
Id term vanishes by log normalization and its derivative tensor is
-kappa integral X tensor grad log L. The source c_i term cancels by
the third identity in (17), and

    Delta/N+Delta/2-(N+2)Delta/(2N)=0.

This independently proves (21), with the displayed tensor orientations.
Taking the trace and subtracting each g_z dot F_z proves (22). The
remaining sum g_z dot F_z need not vanish unless the centroid graph is
affine or another actual argument is supplied. Calling n dot(X-g_z) a
radial speed in that identity does not assert its simultaneous compatible
feasibility.

## 4. Surface reserve and limits of the scope

The first weak derivative of positive finite-PL log L is grad_X L/L a.e.;
there is no crease measure in that FIRST derivative. The finite tangent
extension of -log below each plane's positive minimum, followed by a
finite maximum, is a globally finite convex extension of -log L on C.
Thus the signed convex-potential test used in (24) is admissible under
the stated physical-cone premise.

Given the separate surface convex-order martingale, its Jensen identity
gives exactly R=-integral Xi B. Conditional barycenters and concavity of
L yield d_L>=0. Taylor's inequality for log, with second derivative at
most -1/L_max^2 on the entire positive value range, gives (25) including
the full square about the SOURCE value, not only conditional variance.
Both its terms have the displayed nonnegative signs. The note correctly
keeps the surface d_L distinct from the identically zero volume-row
defects. It does not infer R=0.

The surface martingale existence in Section 6 is the ordinary compact
convex-order coupling dependency already used in the earlier surface-dual
sources; it is not a consequence of the finite-source allocation lemma
alone. All newly computed flux and torque identities are independent of
that optional surface reading.
